verses.text: Joshua was getting very old. The LORD told him, “You're well along in years, and there's still a lot of land to take possession of.
Here's the land that remains: all the territory of the Philistines and all the territory of the Geshurites,

from the Shihor near Egypt north to the border of Ekron, which is counted as Canaanite territory. It includes the territory of the five Philistine rulers in Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron, as well as the Avvim
in the south. There's also all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah, which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek at the Amorite border.
There's the land of the Gebalites and all Lebanon toward the east, from Baal Gad below Mount Hermon to the entrance of Hamath.

I'll drive out the people of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth Maim, including all the Sidonians, ahead of the Israelites. Your job is to assign the land to Israel as an inheritance, just as I told you.
Now divide this land as an inheritance among the nine tribes and the half tribe of Manasseh.”
The other half of Manasseh received its inheritance alongside Reuben and Gad on the east side of the Jordan, just as Moses, the LORD's servant, had assigned it.
It stretched from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley and the town in the middle of the valley, across the whole plain of Medeba as far as Dibon.
It included all the towns of King Sihon of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, as far as the Ammonite border.
It included Gilead, the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites, all of Mount Hermon, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah.
It also included the entire kingdom of Og in Bashan, who ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei and was one of the last of the Rephaim. Moses defeated those kings and drove them out.
The Israelites didn't drive out the Geshurites or Maacathites, so the people of Geshur and Maacath still live among Israel today.
Levi was the only tribe that got no land as an inheritance. Their inheritance was the offerings made by fire to the LORD, the God of Israel, just as he had promised them.
Moses gave land to the tribe of Reuben, clan by clan.
Their territory ran from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, taking in the town in the middle of the valley and the whole plain near Medeba.
It included Heshbon and all its towns on the plain: Dibon, Bamoth Baal, and Beth Baal Meon,
along with Jahaz, Kedemoth, and Mephaath,
Kiriathaim, Sibmah, and Zereth Shahar on the hill in the valley,
Beth Peor, the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth Jeshimoth.

It included all the towns on the plain and the entire kingdom of Sihon, the Amorite king who ruled in Heshbon. Moses defeated him and the Midianite chiefs Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, who were rulers under Sihon and lived in the land.
The Israelites also put Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, to the sword along with the others they killed.
The bank of the Jordan marked Reuben's border. These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the tribe of Reuben, clan by clan.
Moses also gave land to the tribe of Gad, clan by clan.
Their territory included Jazer, all the towns of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites as far as Aroer near Rabbah.
It stretched from Heshbon to Ramath Mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir.

In the valley it included Beth Haram, Beth Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of King Sihon's kingdom in Heshbon. It ran along the east bank of the Jordan as far as the far end of the Sea of Chinnereth.
These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the tribe of Gad, clan by clan.
Moses gave an inheritance to half the tribe of Manasseh, assigning it to their clans.
Their territory stretched from Mahanaim and included all Bashan, the entire kingdom of King Og of Bashan, and all sixty of Jair's settlements in Bashan.
Half of Gilead, along with Ashtaroth and Edrei, the cities of Og's kingdom in Bashan, went to the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh. It was given to half of Machir's descendants, clan by clan.
These are the inheritances Moses assigned on the plains of Moab, east of the Jordan across from Jericho.
Moses gave no land as an inheritance to the tribe of Levi. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, just as he told them.
